objective: The frontend spec creation flow is missing CLI parity (no sequential wizard, no readiness loop), the dashboard home page shows stale/static data, and the UI looks like a generic LLM tool instead of a demo-worthy product that can be recorded as a compelling video.
outcomes: QuestionsStep becomes a one-question-at-a-time stepper: shows current question index (e.g. 2/5), Back/Next buttons, answer persists as user navigates

After submitting the last answer, the modal calls GET /specs/:id/readiness — if ready:true it navigates to the spec; if not it re-fetches GET /specs/:id/questions and shows the remaining questions for another round
The loop continues until readiness returns ready:true or the user explicitly clicks Skip
Dashboard home page fetches live data: total spec count, approved count, verified count, active spec with live readiness score — no hardcoded numbers
All new UI elements use the existing dark-first design system (brand-teal, dark slate backgrounds) with CSS transitions on state changes (opacity, translate) — no new animation libraries
The spec wizard modal shows a readiness score progress bar that animates upward after each answer round

evidence.excerpt: Fill all CLI-parity gaps in the frontend: (1) sequential one-question-at-a-time wizard with readiness re-check loop until ready:true; (2) make the dashboard home page fully dynamic with live stats; (3) make the entire UI visually striking like an action movie trailer — dark, high-contrast, animated, cinematic — not a boring LLM dashboard

edgeCases.scenario: All questions answered but readiness still below threshold
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Show remaining blockers clearly and re-render the next round of questions
Show inline error, keep modal open with a Retry button

edgeCases.scenario: No specs exist on the dashboard
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Show zero-state with a CTA to create the first spec

edgeCases.scenario: Backend is unreachable when dashboard loads
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Show 0 for all counters, no crash

constraints: No new npm packages — use only Tailwind CSS and lucide-react already in the project
CSS animations must use Tailwind transition utilities only (no keyframe imports)
Dashboard page stays a server component (async function) — only add a thin client wrapper for the stats counter if needed
Do not change backend/core, mcp, or the server app.ts
healthMetrics: All existing server tests still pass (pnpm test)
Frontend builds with no TypeScript errors (pnpm build)
verification: Create a new spec — modal shows questions one at a time with progress counter
Answer all questions — modal shows readiness check, then navigates to spec detail
Leave all answers blank — Submit button disabled
Visit dashboard — spec counts and readiness score reflect real backend data
